[cols="2h,5,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Construction |X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 |X25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 |X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305, anonymous

|Names
|`box`
|`box_xchacha20poly1305`
|`sealed_box`

|What it does
|Authenticated encryption between two key pairs: X25519 agrees a key once per pair, then XSalsa20-Poly1305 seals each message; either party can have written it
|The same, with XChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing each message
|Encryption to a public key alone: a key pair drawn per message, whose public key travels with it; the recipient cannot tell who sealed it, and the sender cannot open it afterwards

|Keys
|the own 32-byte secret key and the peer's 32-byte X25519 public key
|the same
|to seal, the recipient's 32-byte public key; to open, the recipient's key pair

|Nonce
|24 bytes, safe to draw at random (link:https://cr.yp.to/snuffle/xsalsa-20081128.pdf[D. J. Bernstein, Extending the Salsa20 nonce, 2008])
|24 bytes, safe to draw at random
|none: derived from the two public keys

|Overhead per message
|a 16-byte tag
|a 16-byte tag
|48 bytes: the ephemeral public key and the tag

|Standards and sources
|link:https://nacl.cr.yp.to/box.html[NaCl, public-key authenticated encryption (crypto_box)], link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/authenticated_encryption[libsodium's documentation, public-key authenticated encryption]
|link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/authenticated_encryption[libsodium's documentation, public-key authenticated encryption]
|link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/sealed_boxes[libsodium's documentation, sealed boxes]

|Choose it when
|two parties who know each other's public keys exchange messages, in NaCl's and libsodium's format; a peer key of small order is refused
|the peer uses libsodium's `crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305`; otherwise `box`, NaCl's format
|anyone may write to a recipient who must not learn who wrote: anonymous feedback, a drop box; it proves nothing about the sender
|===
